# Yuku, a JavaScript/TypeScript Compiler Toolchain in Zig

> Yuku is a JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.
> Full documentation, every page concatenated for LLMs. Index: https://yuku.fyi/llms.txt

# Introduction

Source: https://yuku.fyi/

Yuku is a high-performance JavaScript/TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig. It is designed for correctness, performance, and clarity.

[Try it in the playground →](https://playground.yuku.fyi)

## Why Yuku

**Correct.** Yuku is 100% ECMAScript spec compliant. Zero failures and zero AST mismatches. Read [how Yuku is tested](https://yuku.fyi/testing/).

**Fast.** Built using data-oriented design principles and generous performance engineering, see [Performance](#performance).

**Anywhere.** Node.js, Bun, Deno, browsers, edge runtimes, and native Zig.

**Zero dependencies.** Pure Zig, with no third-party dependencies in the build or on npm.

**Modern.** New and proposed syntax, including decorators, source phase and deferred imports, and `using` declarations.

## JavaScript

```bash
npm install yuku
```

```js
import { parse, print } from "yuku";

const file = parse(`const answer: number = 42;`, { path: "answer.ts" });

print(file, { strip: true }).code; // "const answer = 42;"
```

One import parses, analyzes, walks, builds, renames, and prints. The [package guide](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#readme) documents it.

## Zig

Yuku needs Zig 0.17.0 or later.

```bash
zig fetch --save git+https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku.git
```

```zig
// build.zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize });
my_module.addImport("parser", yuku.module("parser"));
```

```zig
const parser = @import("parser");

var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, "const x: number = 1;", .{ .lang = .ts });
defer tree.deinit();
```

These pages document it: the [parser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/), the [AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/), [semantic analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/), [traversal](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/), and [codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/). To add syntax of your own, see [Dialects](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme).

## Performance

Measured on an Apple M3, with every tool doing the same work.

### Parser

Natively, Yuku parses faster than Oxc and SWC.

![Parsing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) natively · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-native)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-native/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript.svg "Native benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, and SWC parsing typescript.js")

On npm, it parses faster than the alternatives, on small and large files.

![Parsing `react.js` (70 KB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/react.svg "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, SWC, Babel, and Acorn parsing react.js")

![Parsing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript.svg "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, Oxc, SWC, Babel, and Acorn parsing typescript.js")

### Analyzer

Analyzing a whole codebase, resolving every reference and linking every import across files, Yuku is faster than typescript-eslint and the TypeScript API, and on a single large file too.

![Analyzing three.js (755 files) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/three.svg "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, TypeScript, and typescript-eslint analyzing three.js")

![Analyzing `typescript.js` (7.8 MB) on npm · [benchmark](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript_js.svg "npm benchmark comparing Yuku, TypeScript, and typescript-eslint analyzing typescript.js")

# Parser

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/

The parser reads JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSX into a [tree](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/). It recovers from errors, so a parse with diagnostics still returns everything it could read. From JavaScript, see [`parse`](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#parse).

```zig
const std = @import("std");
const parser = @import("parser");

pub fn main() !void {
    var tree = try parser.parse(std.heap.smp_allocator, "const x: number = 1;", .{ .lang = .ts });
    defer tree.deinit();
}
```

```zig
pub fn parse(child_allocator: std.mem.Allocator, source: []const u8, options: Options) error{OutOfMemory}!ast.Tree
```

The tree lives in one arena, which `tree.deinit()` frees, and borrows `source`, which must outlive it.

## Options

| Field             | Default    | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source_type`     | `.module`  | `.script`, `.module`, or `.commonjs`, whose top level is a function body                                                      |
| `lang`            | `.js`      | `.js`, `.ts`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, or `.dts`                                                                                       |
| `preserve_parens` | `true`     | Keep `parenthesized_expression` nodes                                                                                         |
| `comments`        | `.collect` | `.none`, `.collect`, or `.attach`, see [Comments](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#comments)                                                      |
| `tokens`          | `false`    | Keep every token, see [Tokens](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#tokens)                                                                           |
| `dialect`         | `false`    | Read with the [dialect](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme) the build has compiled in |

`ast.Lang.fromPath` and `ast.SourceType.fromPath` read them from a file name.

```zig
const options: parser.Options = .{ .lang = .fromPath(path), .source_type = .fromPath(path) };
```

## Diagnostics

Every part of Yuku reports problems as an `ast.Diagnostic`.

```zig
pub const Diagnostic = struct {
    severity: Severity = .@"error", // .@"error", .warning, .hint, or .info
    message: []const u8,
    span: Span,                     // bytes
    help: ?[]const u8 = null,
    labels: []const Label = &.{},   // .{ .span, .message } pointing at related code
};
```

```zig
for (tree.diagnostics.items) |d| {
    std.debug.print("[{s}] {s} at {d}..{d}\n", .{ d.severity.toString(), d.message, d.span.start, d.span.end });
}

tree.hasErrors();      // any .@"error"
try tree.addDiagnostic(.{ .message = "unused", .span = span });
```

[Semantic analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) adds the early errors that need scopes, such as redeclarations.

# AST

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/

A parse returns an `ast.Tree`, a flat tree whose nodes, child lists, and strings live in arrays in one arena. From JavaScript, the tree decodes to [ESTree](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#the-ast).

| Type         | Is                                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NodeIndex`  | A node's position in `tree.nodes`, `.null` for an absent child |
| `IndexRange` | A child list, a `start` and `len` in `tree.extras`             |
| `String`     | Text, a zero-copy slice of the source or an entry in the pool  |
| `Span`       | A source range in bytes, `start` and `end`                     |

## Reading

```zig
tree.root          // the program node
tree.data(index)   // its payload, a NodeData union
tree.span(index)
tree.extra(range)  // the nodes of a child list
tree.string(text)  // the bytes of a String

tree.source        // also lang and source_type
tree.isTs()        // also isJsx and isModule
```

```zig
switch (tree.data(index)) {
    .variable_declaration => |decl| {
        for (tree.extra(decl.declarators)) |declarator| {
            _ = declarator;
        }
    },
    .identifier_reference => |id| std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{tree.string(id.name)}),
    else => {},
}
```

`NodeData` has a tag per node kind, each the snake_case name of its payload, as in `ts_as_expression: TSAsExpression`. [ast.zig](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/src/parser/ast.zig) defines every one with its fields. To walk the whole tree, use the [traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/).

```zig
data.isExpression()             // also isStatement, isDeclaration, isLiteral, isPattern,
                                // isCallable, isIteration, and isTypeContext

literal.value(&tree)            // a numeric literal's f64
ast.BinaryOperator.fromToken(t) // also toToken and toString, on LogicalOperator,
                                // UnaryOperator, UpdateOperator, and AssignmentOperator
kind.toString()                 // on VariableKind, PropertyKind, Accessibility, and the other kinds
```

## Building and editing

```zig
var tree = ast.Tree.init(allocator, ""); // or the source to edit
defer tree.deinit();

const name = try tree.addString("total"); // interned
const id = try tree.addNode(.{ .identifier_reference = .{ .name = name } }, span);
const list = try tree.addExtra(&.{id});   // a child list

tree.setData(index, data);
tree.setSpan(index, span);
tree.setName(index, name);                // any node a declaration or reference can be
tree.sourceSlice(start, end);             // a String over the source, no copy
tree.allocator();                         // the arena
```

A built tree sets `tree.root` itself. The [transform](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#transform) traverser makes these changes during a walk.

## Comments

`.comments = .collect` keeps every comment in `tree.comments`, in source order. `.attach` also gives each to the node it prints with, so it moves with its node and [codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/) prints it in place.

```zig
pub const Comment = struct {
    type: Type,         // .line or .block
    value: String,      // without delimiters
    span: Span,         // empty for an added comment
    position: Position, // .before, .after, or .inside an otherwise empty node
    same_line: bool,
};
```

```zig
var comments = tree.commentsOf(node);
while (comments.next()) |comment| std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{tree.string(comment.value)});

tree.hasComments(node);
tree.commentsIn(tree.span(node)); // the source comments within a span
try tree.addComment(node, .{ .type = .block, .value = try tree.addString("#__PURE__") });
try tree.moveComments(from, to);  // to .null drops them
```

## Tokens

`.tokens = true` keeps every token in `tree.tokens`, as the parser resolved it, ending with `eof`.

```zig
for (tree.tokens) |token| std.debug.print("{t} {s}\n", .{ token.tag, token.text(tree.source) });
```

```zig
token.span
token.tag                       // an ast.TokenTag
token.len()
token.hasLineTerminatorBefore() // what ASI reads
token.isEscaped()               // also hasInvalidEscape and hasLoneSurrogates

token.tag.toString()            // its spelling, null for literals and names
token.tag.precedence()          // an ast.Precedence, 0 when none
token.tag.isKeyword()           // also isReserved, isUnconditionallyReserved, isStrictModeReserved,
                                // isIdentifierLike, isNumericLiteral, isBinaryOperator,
                                // isLogicalOperator, isUnaryOperator, and isAssignmentOperator

tree.tokensIn(tree.span(node))  // a node's tokens, a contiguous run
```

Every node but `program`, `template_element`, and `jsx_empty_expression` starts and ends on a token boundary.

## Lexical grammar

`parser.lexical` answers as the lexer does, on UTF-8 names with escapes decoded.

```zig
lexical.isValidIdentifier("class"); // false, reserved, as is await
lexical.isEvalOrArguments("eval");  // true, which strict code cannot bind
lexical.isIdentifierName("class");  // true, reserved words included
lexical.isIdentifierStart('$');     // also isIdentifierChar and isJSXIdentifierChar
lexical.keyword("yield");           // ?TokenTag, contextual keywords included
lexical.lineBreakLen(source, i);    // 0, or the byte length of the line terminator at i

try lexical.decodeStringEscapes(gpa, raw, &out); // appends WTF-8
try lexical.decodeJSXEntities(gpa, raw, &out);
```

# Semantic Analysis

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/

Semantic analysis builds a model of a program's scopes, symbols, and references, with each reference resolved to the symbol it names, and reports the early errors that need scopes, such as redeclarations. From JavaScript, see [Semantic analysis](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#semantic-analysis).

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, source, .{});
defer tree.deinit();

const semantic = try parser.semantic.analyze(&tree, .{ .check = true });
```

```zig
pub fn analyze(tree: *ast.Tree, options: AnalyzeOptions) error{OutOfMemory}!Semantic // .{ .check: bool }
pub fn check(tree: *ast.Tree) error{OutOfMemory}!void
```

- `.check = true` appends the early errors to `tree.diagnostics` in the same walk, and `.check = false` skips their cost.
- `check` reports the same errors faster, without the model.
- The model lives in the tree's arena and describes the tree as parsed. Analyze again after a transform with `.check = false`, since the errors are already reported.
- The [semantic traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#semantic) runs hooks of your own during the analysis.

## The model

```zig
semantic.symbolOf(node)             // ?SymbolId, what a node declares or refers to
semantic.referenceOf(node)          // ?ReferenceId, at an identifier
semantic.scopeOf(node)              // ScopeId, the scope a node creates, or the innermost around it
semantic.parentOf(node)             // ?ast.NodeIndex
semantic.ancestors(node)            // the node, then each parent up to the root

semantic.symbol(id)                 // also reference(id) and scopes.get(id)
semantic.decls(symbol)              // each declaration's name node, in source order
semantic.uses(symbol)               // each ReferenceId to it, in source order

semantic.bindings(scope)            // an iterator over the symbols a scope declares, in no order
semantic.binding(scope, "x")        // ?SymbolId, declared there or a var hoisting through
semantic.lookup(scope, "x", .value) // ?SymbolId, as the name resolves from the scope
semantic.member(ns, "x", .value)    // ?SymbolId, ns.x of a namespace or enum, across merged bodies

semantic.symbols                    // every Symbol, indexed by SymbolId, also references
semantic.scopes.list                // every Scope, indexed by ScopeId
semantic.scopes.ancestors(id)       // a scope, then each parent
```

The types are in `parser.semantic`. Ids are dense, with symbols ordered by first declaration and references by position.

```zig
pub const Symbol = struct {
    name: ast.String,
    flags: Flags,   // see Symbols
    scope: ScopeId, // where it lands, the hoist target for a var
};

pub const Reference = struct {
    name: ast.String,
    scope: ScopeId,
    node: ast.NodeIndex, // an identifier_reference, jsx_identifier, or identifier_name
    symbol: SymbolId,    // .none for a global or undeclared name
    flags: Flags,        // .write, .space, and .type_position
};

pub const Scope = struct {
    node: ast.NodeIndex,
    parent: ScopeId,       // .none at the root
    hoist_target: ScopeId,
    kind: Kind,            // .global, .module, .function, .function_body, .block, .class,
                           // .static_block, .expression_name, or .ts_module
    flags: Flags,          // .strict
};
```

`ScopeId.root` is the global scope, and `semantic.scopeOf(tree.root)` the scope of top-level code, the module scope in a module. A JSX component tag and a type predicate's parameter are references too, so a rename sees every use.

```zig
const name = try tree.addString("renamed");
for (semantic.decls(symbol)) |node| tree.setName(node, name);
for (semantic.uses(symbol)) |id| tree.setName(semantic.reference(id).node, name);
```

An enum member is also read as `E.member`, a member access rather than a reference, so a rename of one is incomplete.

```zig
for (semantic.symbols, 0..) |symbol, i| {
    const id: parser.semantic.SymbolId = @fromBackingInt(@intCast(i));
    if (semantic.uses(id).len == 0) std.debug.print("unused {s}\n", .{tree.string(symbol.name)});
}

for (semantic.references) |reference| {
    if (reference.symbol == .none) std.debug.print("undeclared {s}\n", .{tree.string(reference.name)});
}
```

## Scopes

The scope tree follows the specification.

- A catch clause shares its scope with its body, unless its parameter has a default value or a computed key.
- A named function or class expression has a scope of its own for its name.
- A function body scopes its `let` and `const` apart from the parameters, as TypeScript does.
- A class decorator sees the scope around its class, and a member decorator sees the class scope.
- Strict mode comes from modules, classes, and `"use strict"` directives.

## Symbols

`symbol.flags` records its declaration kinds and modifiers.

| Kinds                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Modifiers                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `function_scoped_var`, `block_scoped_var`, `function`, `class`, `regular_enum`, `const_enum`, `value_module`, `interface`, `type_alias`, `type_parameter`, `namespace_module`, `import`, `type_import` | `const_var`, `ambient`, `parameter`, `catch_var`, `exported`, `is_default`, `enum_member` |

```zig
symbol.flags.intersects(Symbol.value_space) // also variable, any_import, type_space, and namespace_space
symbol.flags.visibleIn(.type)               // whether a reference in a space binds to it, always for an import
symbol.flags.isHoistingVar()
symbol.flags.toString()
```

One rule decides merging and redeclaration. Each declaration kind has an exclusion mask in `Symbol.Excludes`, and a new declaration conflicts with a symbol whose flags intersect it, or merges into it otherwise. Function overloads, a `class` and an `interface`, and a `namespace` and an `enum` merge this way, and a namespace or enum declared in several blocks sees the members of the others. A conflicting declaration is still one of the symbol's `decls`.

## Declaration spaces

A name resolves in one space, and a binding outside that space does not shadow it, as in TypeScript.

```ts
type T = string;
function f() {
  const T = 1;
  let x: T; // the outer type T
  T;        // the inner const T
}
```

| Space        | For                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `.value`     | Runtime uses                                      |
| `.type`      | Annotations                                       |
| `.namespace` | The head of a dotted name, such as `ns` in `ns.T` |
| `.typeof`    | A value in a type, such as `x` in `typeof x`      |
| `.any`       | Alias positions, such as `export { x }`           |

`lookup` resolves by scope alone, without the position rules a reference follows, such as an `infer` type parameter being visible only in its true branch.

## Module records

`module_record.collect` lists a module's imports and exports, as the specification's ImportEntry and ExportEntry records with the symbol behind each, static ones first and then dynamic ones, each in source order.

```zig
const records = try parser.semantic.module_record.collect(&tree, &semantic);
```

```zig
pub const Import = struct {
    kind: Kind,               // .named, .namespace, .side_effect, .import_equals, .dynamic,
                              // .require, or .augmentation
    name: ast.String,         // the imported name, "default" for a default import
    symbol: SymbolId,         // the binding it declares, .none if it declares none
    specifier: ast.String,
    type_only: bool,
    phase: ?ast.ImportPhase,  // .source or .@"defer"
    node: ast.NodeIndex,
    scope: ScopeId,           // the body of an augmentation
};

pub const Export = struct {
    kind: Kind,               // .named, .re_export, .namespace, .star, .equals, or .global
    name: ast.String,
    symbol: SymbolId,         // the binding it exports, .none for a re-export
    from_name: ast.String,    // the name a re_export takes
    specifier: ast.String,
    type_only: bool,
    node: ast.NodeIndex,
};

records.flags // .uses_require, .uses_module, .uses_exports, and .uses_import_meta
```

- A dynamic `import()` or `require()` counts when its specifier is a string, or a template with no substitutions.
- An `augmentation` is a `declare module "m"` block in a module, which merges its body's declarations into `m`.
- A declaration file that is a module with no export statement exports every declaration but its imports, as in TypeScript.
- `flags` record free uses, so a local `require` does not count.

# Traverse

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/

The traverser walks a tree depth-first and calls a visitor's hooks at each node, in one of four modes. From JavaScript, see [`walk`](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#walk).

| Mode                      | Tracks                          | Returns                                   | `ctx.tree`        |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| [`basic`](#visitors)      | the path from the root          | nothing                                   | `*const ast.Tree` |
| [`scoped`](#scoped)       | the path and lexical scopes     | a `ScopeTree`                             | `*const ast.Tree` |
| [`semantic`](#semantic)   | scopes, symbols, and references | the [`Semantic`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) model | `*const ast.Tree` |
| [`transform`](#transform) | the path                        | nothing                                   | `*ast.Tree`       |

```zig
pub fn traverse(comptime V: type, tree: *ast.Tree, visitor: *V) std.mem.Allocator.Error!Result
```

`basic.traverse` takes a `*const ast.Tree`. Every mode can fail with `error.OutOfMemory`, since a subtree deeper than 256 levels walks iteratively.

## Visitors

A visitor is a struct of `pub` hooks named after node tags. This one counts functions.

```zig
const std = @import("std");
const parser = @import("parser");
const ast = parser.ast;
const traverser = parser.traverser;
const basic = traverser.basic;

const Counter = struct {
    functions: u32 = 0,

    pub fn enter_function(self: *Counter, _: ast.Function, _: ast.NodeIndex, _: *basic.Ctx) traverser.Action {
        self.functions += 1;
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var counter = Counter{};
try basic.traverse(Counter, &tree, &counter);
```

```zig
pub fn enter_<tag>(self: *V, payload: ast.<Payload>, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *Ctx) Action
pub fn exit_<tag>(self: *V, payload: ast.<Payload>, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *Ctx) void
pub fn enter_node(self: *V, data: ast.NodeData, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *Ctx) Action
pub fn exit_node(self: *V, data: ast.NodeData, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *Ctx) void
```

- An enter hook returns an `Action`, or `std.mem.Allocator.Error!Action` to `try` an allocation.
- A misspelled hook or a wrong payload type is a compile error. A hook that is not `pub` is never called.
- At each node, `enter_node` runs, then `enter_<tag>` unless `enter_node` returned something other than `.proceed`, then the children in field order, then `exit_<tag>` and `exit_node`.
- A [dialect's](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme) nodes reach `enter_dialect` and `exit_dialect` with an `ast.Dialect`.

| `Action`   | Effect                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.proceed` | Walk into the children                                             |
| `.skip`    | Pass over the children. The node's exit hooks still run.           |
| `.stop`    | End the walk. Exit hooks still run for the node and its ancestors. |

Every mode's context has `ctx.tree` and `ctx.path`.

```zig
ctx.path.parent()     // ?ast.NodeIndex
ctx.path.ancestor(n)  // with the current node at 0
ctx.path.ancestors()  // an iterator from the current node up
ctx.path.depth()      // 1 at the root
```

## Scoped

`ctx.scope` follows the walk into and out of every scope, and the walk returns every scope it saw as a `ScopeTree`. A node's own scope is current in its enter hook. This lint counts each `var` that escapes its block.

```zig
const scoped = traverser.scoped;

const VarInBlock = struct {
    found: u32 = 0,

    pub fn enter_variable_declaration(self: *VarInBlock, decl: ast.VariableDeclaration, _: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *scoped.Ctx) traverser.Action {
        if (decl.kind == .@"var" and ctx.scope.get(ctx.scope.current).kind == .block) self.found += 1;
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var lint = VarInBlock{};
const scopes = try scoped.traverse(VarInBlock, &tree, &lint);
```

```zig
ctx.scope.current        // the current ScopeId
ctx.scope.get(id)        // its Scope, with kind, hoist_target, and flags.strict
ctx.scope.ancestors(id)  // an iterator from a scope up
```

## Semantic

The walk builds the [`Semantic`](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/) model and returns it. A binding is declared after its node's enter hook, and references resolve when the walk ends, so a visitor collects nodes and queries the model after. This one finds the types a file imports.

```zig
const sem = traverser.semantic;

const TypeNames = struct {
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    nodes: std.ArrayList(ast.NodeIndex) = .empty,

    pub fn enter_identifier_reference(self: *TypeNames, _: ast.IdentifierReference, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *sem.Ctx) std.mem.Allocator.Error!traverser.Action {
        if (ctx.inTypePosition()) try self.nodes.append(self.allocator, index);
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var names = TypeNames{ .allocator = tree.allocator() };
const semantic = try sem.traverse(TypeNames, &tree, &names);

for (names.nodes.items) |node| {
    const id = semantic.symbolOf(node) orelse continue; // a global type
    if (semantic.symbol(id).flags.intersects(parser.semantic.Symbol.any_import)) std.debug.print("imported\n", .{});
}
```

```zig
ctx.inTypePosition()
ctx.inTsNamespace()
ctx.scope                          // as in scoped
ctx.symbols.binding(scope, name)   // ?SymbolId, a name declared so far
ctx.symbols.ownBinding(scope, name)
ctx.symbols.symbol(id)
```

The model covers the whole tree, so `.skip` and `.stop` only mute the visitor.

## Transform

`ctx.tree` is mutable, and the walker reads a node again after its enter hook, so it walks a replacement. This one turns `price + tax` into `price * tax`.

```zig
const transform = traverser.transform;

const AddToMultiply = struct {
    pub fn enter_binary_expression(_: *AddToMultiply, expr: ast.BinaryExpression, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *transform.Ctx) traverser.Action {
        if (expr.operator == .add) {
            ctx.tree.setData(index, .{ .binary_expression = .{
                .left = expr.left,
                .right = expr.right,
                .operator = .multiply,
            } });
        }
        return .proceed;
    }
};

var rewrite = AddToMultiply{};
try transform.traverse(AddToMultiply, &tree, &rewrite);
```

- The tree's [building and editing](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#building-and-editing) calls work during the walk.
- A node whose tag a hook changes is walked, and exited, as its new kind.
- After wrapping a node in a new parent, return `.skip`, so the walk does not enter it again.

Modes compose as passes, such as a transform and then a semantic walk of its result.

## Your own mode

A mode is a context type over one walker.

```zig
pub fn walk(comptime C: type, comptime V: type, visitor: *V, ctx: *C, comptime options: traverser.Options) std.mem.Allocator.Error!void
```

A context has a `tree` field, a `*ast.Tree` to edit or a `*const ast.Tree` to read, and an optional `path: traverser.NodePath`, which its `enter` and `exit` push and pop. The walk calls these optional methods around the visitor's hooks, with the tag known at compile time.

```zig
pub fn enter(self: *C, comptime tag: ast.NodeTag, index: ast.NodeIndex, data: ast.NodeData) std.mem.Allocator.Error!void
pub fn post_enter(self: *C, comptime tag: ast.NodeTag, index: ast.NodeIndex, data: ast.NodeData) std.mem.Allocator.Error!void
pub fn exit(self: *C, comptime tag: ast.NodeTag, index: ast.NodeIndex, data: ast.NodeData) void
```

`.whole_tree = true` calls the context for every node, even under a `.skip`, so a context that builds a model of the whole tree sees all of it. [basic.zig](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/src/parser/traverser/basic.zig) is the smallest mode.

# Codegen

Source: https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/

Codegen prints a tree back to source, with optional type stripping, minification, and source maps. From JavaScript, see [`print`](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#print).

```zig
var tree = try parser.parse(allocator, "const x: number = 1;", .{ .lang = .ts });
defer tree.deinit();

const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{ .strip = true });
defer result.deinit(allocator);

std.debug.print("{s}\n", .{result.code}); // const x = 1;
```

```zig
pub fn generate(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, tree: *const ast.Tree, options: Options) error{OutOfMemory}!Result

pub const Result = struct {
    code: []const u8,
    diagnostics: []const ast.Diagnostic, // what strip could not print
    map: ?SourceMap = null,

    pub fn deinit(self: Result, allocator: std.mem.Allocator) void
};
```

`generate` prints from `tree.root` and leaves the tree unchanged. The result belongs to `allocator`.

## Options

| Field        | Default     | Description                                                           |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `strip`      | `false`     | Print TypeScript as JavaScript, see [Type stripping](#type-stripping) |
| `minify`     | `false`     | Rewrite syntax to shorter forms, see [Minification](#minification)    |
| `format`     | `.pretty`   | `.pretty`, or `.compact` with only the whitespace the grammar needs   |
| `indent`     | `2`         | Spaces per level in the pretty format                                 |
| `quotes`     | `.preserve` | `.preserve`, `.double`, `.single`, or `.shortest`                     |
| `comments`   | `.some`     | `.some`, `.all`, `.none`, `.line`, or `.block`                        |
| `source_map` | `null`      | A `SourceMapOptions`, see [Source maps](#source-maps)                 |

Comments print from the nodes they are [attached to](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#comments), so parse with `.comments = .attach` to keep them. `.some` keeps the block comments bundlers keep: those opening with `!` or `*`, those whose text starts with `@` or `#`, and those holding `@license`, `@preserve`, or `@cc_on`.

## Type stripping

`strip` prints TypeScript as JavaScript. Types, interfaces, type aliases, generics, assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`, `declare`, and `abstract` strip cleanly. `enum`, `namespace`, `export =`, `import = require()`, and parameter properties need new runtime code, so they are left out and reported in `diagnostics`. Their ambient forms strip silently.

## Minification

`minify` rewrites syntax, and with `.compact` and `.shortest` it fully minifies.

```zig
const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{
    .minify = true,
    .format = .compact,
    .quotes = .shortest,
});
// const enabled = true; const size = 1000000;
// prints as const enabled=!0;const size=1e6
```

- `true` and `false` become `!0` and `!1`.
- Numbers take their shortest form, so `1000000` becomes `1e6` and `0.5` becomes `.5`.
- `obj["foo"]` becomes `obj.foo`, and a quoted key such as `{ "foo": x }` becomes `{ foo: x }`, where that keeps the meaning.
- `</script`, `<!--`, and `-->` are escaped in strings and untagged templates, so the output is safe inside a `<script>` tag.

## Source maps

```zig
const result = try parser.codegen.generate(allocator, &tree, .{
    .source_map = .{
        .file = "out.js",
        .source_file_name = "in.js",
        .source_root = null,
        .sources_content = source,
    },
});
defer result.deinit(allocator);

const map = result.map.?;
```

```zig
pub const SourceMap = struct {
    version: u8 = 3,
    file: ?[]const u8,                     // borrowed from the options
    source_root: ?[]const u8,              // borrowed from the options
    sources: []const []const u8,           // one entry
    sources_content: ?[]const ?[]const u8,
    names: []const []const u8,             // empty
    mappings: []const u8,                  // VLQ
};
```

Columns are UTF-16 code units, as browsers and source map libraries expect. Written as JSON, `source_root` and `sources_content` take the Source Map V3 keys `sourceRoot` and `sourcesContent`.

A build that never needs maps compiles them out, and `map` is then always `null`.

```zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{ .@"codegen-source-maps" = false });
```

# Testing

Source: https://yuku.fyi/testing/

Yuku is tested for spec conformance, exact AST shapes, codegen soundness, and behavior under memory pressure.

## The parser test suite

The parser runs against [parser-test-suite](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/parser-test-suite), over 57,000 tests from [Test262](https://github.com/tc39/test262), the [TypeScript](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript) compiler, and [Babel](https://github.com/babel/babel), synced with upstream daily.

| Category   | Expectation                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pass`     | Parses with no diagnostics, and the AST matches a snapshot exactly |
| `fail`     | Produces a syntax error                                            |
| `semantic` | Parses, then fails semantic analysis with an early error           |

The snapshots come from an independent parser, [Oxc](https://oxc.rs), and must match down to every field, position, and comment. Passing files must also walk in source order and pass semantic analysis without a false positive. Yuku passes every test.

The suite runs through the `yuku` package built from local source, so it checks the whole chain from the Zig parser to the JavaScript AST.

## Codegen

Every parseable file in the suite is printed under several option sets. Each output must parse again, plain output must reparse to the same AST, and printing must be a fixed point with no comment lost or duplicated. The Zig and JavaScript printers must agree byte for byte, and every identifier in a source map must trace back to its original name and position.

## Semantic analysis

Every file in the suite is analyzed, along with real codebases pinned to a commit, such as the TypeScript compiler, Node.js, Vue, and three.js. The TypeScript checker must resolve every reference, values and types alike, to the same declaration as Yuku. [@typescript-eslint/scope-manager](https://typescript-eslint.io/packages/scope-manager) must agree on every runtime reference and write, and on every declaration and its scope. Each runs over a million comparisons.

Each codebase is also linked as one project, and every import, re-export, exported name, and relative path must resolve as in a TypeScript program.

## Fuzzing

A fuzzer throws millions of adversarial inputs at the parser in every language mode, injecting out-of-memory failures along the way. The parser must never crash, and any failure dumps a self-contained reproducer. With everything in one arena, a parse has nothing to leak even when memory runs out.

## Running the suites

```bash
bun run test
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) to run one suite or add cases.

# Security

Source: https://yuku.fyi/security/

Yuku processes source code that may be attacker controlled, so it treats every input as untrusted.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue. Report privately through GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/security/advisories/new), or email [arshadpyaseen@gmail.com](mailto:arshadpyaseen@gmail.com).

We aim to acknowledge reports within 72 hours. Please allow a reasonable window for a fix before public disclosure. We are glad to credit you in the advisory. Fixes ship against the latest version.

## Our practices

- **No third-party dependencies.** The npm package has none and runs no install scripts, and the Zig build has none.
- **Provenance publishing.** Releases publish to npm with provenance through OIDC trusted publishing, with no long-lived tokens.
- **Hardened CI.** Every action is pinned to a commit hash, workflow tokens are read-only by default, and [zizmor](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor) and [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://securityscorecards.dev) check the workflows.
- **Reproducible builds.** Installs use a frozen lockfile.
- **Memory safety.** A parse allocates everything in one arena and frees it in one step. Where the npm package runs Yuku as WebAssembly, it is also sandboxed from host memory.
- **Fuzzing.** Millions of adversarial inputs per run, see [Testing](https://yuku.fyi/testing/#fuzzing).

# JavaScript

Source: https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#readme

```bash
npm install yuku
```

It runs natively where its addon for the platform installs, and as WebAssembly everywhere else. Cloudflare Workers and Vercel Edge run WebAssembly only from a file, so there also install `@yuku-toolchain/wasm`.

```js
import { js, parse, print, walk } from "yuku";

const file = parse(`const area = radius ** 2 * Math.PI;`);

walk(file.program, {
  BinaryExpression(node, ctx) {
    if (node.operator === "**") ctx.replace(js`Math.pow(${node.left}, ${node.right})`);
  },
});

print(file).code; // "const area = Math.pow(radius, 2) * Math.PI;"
```

```js
const file = parse(`const double = (n) => n * 2;\ndouble(21);`, { semantic: true });

const double = file.rootScope.find("double");
double.references.length; // 1
double.rename("twice");   // [], no conflicts, so it renamed

print(file).code; // "const twice = (n) => n * 2;\ntwice(21);"
```

- [Parse](#parse): [options](#options), [diagnostics](#diagnostics), [comments](#comments), [tokens](#tokens)
- [The AST](#the-ast)
- [Walk](#walk): [the context](#the-context), [editing](#editing), [async work](#async-work)
- [Templates](#templates)
- [Utils](#utils)
- [Semantic analysis](#semantic-analysis): [scopes](#scopes), [bindings](#bindings), [references](#references), [imports and exports](#imports-and-exports)
- [Rename](#rename)
- [Projects](#projects)
- [Print](#print)
- [Performance](#performance)

## Parse

`parse` reads JavaScript, TypeScript, or JSX, from a string or UTF-8 bytes, into a `SourceFile`.

```js
import { parse } from "yuku";

const file = parse(source, { path: "src/app.tsx" });

file.program;     // the ESTree / TypeScript-ESTree Program
file.comments;    // every comment, in source order
file.diagnostics;
file.source;
file.path;
file.lang;        // "tsx", from the path
file.sourceType;  // "module"
```

The parser recovers from errors, so a file with diagnostics still has a program.

### Options

| Option           | Default                                             | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`           | none                                                | Names the file, and sets `lang` and `sourceType`                                                                                          |
| `lang`           | from `path`, else `"js"`                            | `"js"`, `"jsx"`, `"ts"`, `"tsx"`, or `"dts"`                                                                                              |
| `sourceType`     | `"commonjs"` for `.cjs` and `.cts`, else `"module"` | `"module"`, `"script"`, or `"commonjs"`                                                                                                   |
| `preserveParens` | `true`                                              | Keep `ParenthesizedExpression` nodes                                                                                                      |
| `attachComments` | `false`                                             | Attach each comment to its node, see [Comments](#comments)                                                                                |
| `tokens`         | `false`                                             | Collect `file.tokens`                                                                                                                     |
| `semantic`       | `false`                                             | Build the [semantic model](#semantic-analysis)                                                                                            |
| `semanticErrors` | `false`                                             | Also report the early errors that need scopes, such as redeclarations                                                                     |
| `core`           | the core yuku ships                                 | The Zig core to run, such as one with a [dialect](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme) compiled in |

A file holds what it was parsed with, so reading `file.tokens` or the model of a file parsed without them throws.

### Diagnostics

Every part of Yuku reports problems in the code in one shape, and throws only when called wrongly.

```ts
interface Diagnostic {
  severity: "error" | "warning" | "hint" | "info";
  message: string;
  path: string | null;
  start: number; // UTF-16 offsets, like nodes
  end: number;
  labels: { start: number; end: number; message: string }[];
  help: string | null;
}
```

```js
for (const { start, message } of file.diagnostics) {
  const { line, column } = file.locate(start);
  console.log(`${file.path}:${line}:${column + 1} ${message}`);
}
```

### Comments

`file.comments` lists every comment as `{ type, value, start, end }`. With `attachComments: true`, each also belongs to the node it prints with.

```js
const { program } = parse(`// header\nfunction foo() {} // trailing`, { attachComments: true });

program.body[0].comments;
// [
//   { type: "Line", value: " header", start: 0, end: 9, position: "before", sameLine: false },
//   { type: "Line", value: " trailing", start: 28, end: 39, position: "after", sameLine: true },
// ]
```

[`print`](#print) prints from `node.comments`, so comments move with their nodes.

### Tokens

`file.tokens` is a `TokenList`, where a token is an index.

```js
import { parse, TokenKind } from "yuku";

const { tokens } = parse(source, { tokens: true });

for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) {
  if (tokens.kind(i) === TokenKind.Arrow) console.log(tokens.start(i), tokens.text(i));
}
```

```js
tokens.kind(i)                      // one of TokenKind
tokens.text(i)
tokens.start(i)                     // UTF-16 offsets
tokens.end(i)

tokens.isKeyword(i)
tokens.isReserved(i)
tokens.isUnconditionallyReserved(i)
tokens.isStrictModeReserved(i)
tokens.isIdentifierLike(i)
tokens.isNumericLiteral(i)
tokens.isBinaryOperator(i)
tokens.isLogicalOperator(i)
tokens.isUnaryOperator(i)
tokens.isAssignmentOperator(i)
tokens.precedence(i)

tokens.newlineBefore(i)
tokens.escaped(i)
tokens.invalidEscape(i)
tokens.loneSurrogate(i)

tokens.range(node)                  // [from, to) of the tokens inside a node
tokens.before(offset)               // the last token ending at or before an offset
tokens.after(offset)                // the first token starting at or after it
tokens.at(offset)                   // the token containing it
```

The queries return an index, or `-1` when there is none.

## The AST

The program is plain objects: [ESTree](https://github.com/estree/estree) for JavaScript and JSX, and [TypeScript-ESTree](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree) for TypeScript, matching [Oxc](https://oxc.rs) down to every field. Every node has `start` and `end` in UTF-16 offsets, and the package exports the type of every node.

```ts
import type { CallExpression, Expression, Node, Program } from "yuku";
```

## Walk

`walk` visits a node and everything under it, depth-first in source order.

```js
import { walk } from "yuku";

walk(file.program, {
  Identifier(node, ctx) {},
  CallExpression: {
    enter(node, ctx) {},
    leave(node, ctx) {},
  },
  Function(node) {}, // declarations, expressions, and arrows
  enter(node) {},    // every node
  leave(node) {},
});
```

Handlers are keyed by node `type`, by alias (`Expression`, `Statement`, `Declaration`, `ModuleDeclaration`, `Function`, `Class`, `Method`, `Loop`, `Pattern`, `JSX`, `TSType`), or by `enter` and `leave`. A list of visitors walks in one pass.

```js
walk(file.program, [noDebugger, noConsole, preferConst]);
```

### The context

```js
ctx.parent;      // null at the walk root
ctx.key;         // the field of the parent holding it
ctx.index;       // its index in an array field, or null
ctx.ancestors(); // from the root down to the parent
```

The [semantic model](#semantic-analysis) answers for any node a walk visits, as `file.scopeOf(node)`, `file.bindingOf(node)`, and `file.referenceOf(node)`.

### Editing

| Call                     | Effect                                                               |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ctx.skip()`             | Skip the children                                                    |
| `ctx.stop()`             | End the walk                                                         |
| `ctx.replace(node)`      | Put a node, or a list in an array field, in its place, then visit it |
| `ctx.remove()`           | Remove it                                                            |
| `ctx.insertBefore(node)` | Insert a sibling the walk passes over                                |
| `ctx.insertAfter(node)`  | Insert a sibling the walk visits next                                |

```js
walk(file.program, {
  DebuggerStatement(node, ctx) {
    ctx.remove();
  },
});
```

### Async work

A walk runs synchronously. For async work, collect the nodes in one walk, await them together, and edit in a second.

```js
const calls = [];
walk(file.program, { CallExpression: (node) => calls.push(node) });

const results = new Map(await Promise.all(calls.map(async (node) => [node, await rewrite(node)])));

walk(file.program, {
  CallExpression(node, ctx) {
    const result = results.get(node);
    if (result !== undefined) ctx.replace(result);
  },
});
```

## Templates

`js` and `ts` build nodes from code, an expression unless it ends in `;`.

```js
import { js, ts } from "yuku";

js`console.log(${node})`;
js`return ${value} ?? ${fallback};`;
ts`const total: ${type} = ${initial};`;
js`import config from "${path}";`;
js`<${tag} label="${label}">{${child}}</${tag}>`;
```

| A hole takes                         | And becomes                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| a node                               | that node                                   |
| a string                             | a name, valid as an identifier or JSX name  |
| a string or number, inside quotes    | its text, escaped as the quotes need        |
| a number, boolean, bigint, or `null` | its literal                                 |
| `undefined`                          | the identifier `undefined`                  |
| an array                             | its items, filling a list such as arguments |

A hole stands for the largest node around it that holds nothing else, such as a statement in `${s};`, a declarator in `let ${d};`, or a property in `{ ${p} }`, and a node of that kind takes its place. A name or a binding pattern fills it instead, and so does an expression in a statement. A hole in a name that holds more, such as `(${p}: T)`, takes a name and keeps the rest. A node that fits neither throws.

Code that needs a function or a generator, such as `return x;` or `yield x`, builds as it would inside one. A node that only exists inside another comes from a template of its container.

```js
js`({ ${key}: ${value} })`.properties[0]; // a property
js`switch (x) { case ${test}: }`.cases[0]; // a case
ts`type _ = Array<${item}>;`.typeAnnotation; // a type
js`{ ${a}; ${b}; }`.body; // several statements
```

A node goes in once, and a copy of it wherever else it is used. The comments around a hole move to what fills it. A template parses once per call site, and its nodes have no position.

## Utils

`yuku/utils` has the small helpers.

```js
import { is, isIdentifierName, isValidIdentifier, unwrap } from "yuku/utils";

is.CallExpression(node);
is.Expression(node);              // aliases too
is.oneOf(node, ["FunctionDeclaration", "ClassDeclaration"]);
is.StringLiteral(node);           // also NumericLiteral, BooleanLiteral, NullLiteral,
                                  // BigIntLiteral, and RegExpLiteral
is.StaticMemberExpression(node);  // also ComputedMemberExpression and PrivateFieldExpression
is.Directive(node);
is.Wrapper(node);                 // parentheses or an erased TypeScript assertion
unwrap(node);                     // the expression inside every wrapper

isValidIdentifier("class");       // false, reserved
isIdentifierName("class");        // true
```

It also has `isIdentifierStart`, `isIdentifierChar`, `isKeyword`, `isReservedWord`, `isStrictReservedWord`, and `isEvalOrArguments`.

## Semantic analysis

The semantic model resolves every name in a file, values and types alike, as the TypeScript checker does.

```js
const file = parse(source, { path: "app.ts", semantic: true });

file.scopes;               // by id, the global scope first
file.rootScope;            // the module scope, or the global scope of a script
file.bindings;             // by id
file.references;           // in source order
file.imports;
file.exports;
file.moduleFlags;          // { usesRequire, usesModule, usesExports, usesImportMeta }

file.bindingOf(node);      // the binding it declares or refers to
file.referenceOf(node);
file.scopeOf(node);
file.capturesOf(fn);       // [{ binding, references, isWritten }]
file.parentOf(node);
file.ancestors(node);      // the node, then each parent up to the root
file.nodeAt(offset);
```

### Scopes

```js
scope.kind;        // "global" | "module" | "function" | "functionBody" | "block" | "class"
                   // | "staticBlock" | "expressionName" | "tsModule"
scope.strict;
scope.node;
scope.parent;
scope.hoistTarget; // where a var declared in it lands
scope.bindings;

scope.find("x");           // a binding it declares
scope.lookup("x", "type"); // resolves a name as code in it would, "value" by default
scope.contains(other);
scope.ancestors();
```

### Bindings

```js
binding.name;
binding.scope;
binding.declarations; // each declaration's name node
binding.references;   // its uses in this file
binding.import;       // the import that declares it
binding.flags;        // a BindingFlags bitset

binding.has(BindingFlags.Function);
binding.has(BindingFlags.Class | BindingFlags.Interface); // any of them
binding.visibleIn("type");

binding.definition();     // { file, binding, augmentations }, following imports
binding.findReferences(); // its uses across a project
binding.rename("next");
```

| Flag                     | Set on                                  |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `FunctionScopedVariable` | `var`, a parameter, or a catch variable |
| `BlockScopedVariable`    | `let`, `const`, `using`, `await using`  |
| `Function`               | a function                              |
| `Class`                  | a class                                 |
| `RegularEnum`            | `enum`                                  |
| `ConstEnum`              | `const enum`                            |
| `ValueModule`            | a namespace with runtime content        |
| `Interface`              | `interface`                             |
| `TypeAlias`              | `type`                                  |
| `TypeParameter`          | `<T>`, `infer T`, a mapped type key     |
| `NamespaceModule`        | a namespace of any kind                 |
| `ValueImport`            | `import x`, `import { x }`              |
| `TypeImport`             | `import type`, `import { type x }`      |
| `Const`                  | `const`, `using`, `await using`         |
| `Ambient`                | `declare`                               |
| `Parameter`              | a parameter                             |
| `CatchVariable`          | `catch (e)`                             |
| `Exported`               | `export`, or implicitly in ambient code |
| `Default`                | `export default <declaration>`          |
| `EnumMember`             | an enum member                          |
| `Variable`               | any variable                            |
| `Import`                 | any import                              |
| `ValueSpace`             | anything visible at runtime             |
| `TypeSpace`              | anything usable as a type               |
| `NamespaceSpace`         | what a dotted type name can start from  |

### References

```js
reference.name;
reference.node;           // the Identifier or JSXIdentifier
reference.scope;
reference.binding;        // null for a global or undeclared name
reference.space;          // "value" | "type" | "namespace" | "typeof" | "any"
reference.inTypePosition;
reference.isWrite;        // x = 1, x++, for (x of xs)
```

### Imports and exports

```js
imp.kind;         // "named" | "namespace" | "sideEffect" | "importEquals" | "dynamic"
                  // | "require" | "augmentation"
imp.name;         // "default" for a default import
imp.local;        // the binding it declares
imp.specifier;
imp.typeOnly;
imp.phase;        // "source" | "defer" | null
imp.node;
imp.resolvedFile; // in a project

exp.kind;         // "named" | "reExport" | "namespace" | "star" | "equals" | "global"
exp.name;         // N for export as namespace N, null for star and equals
exp.local;        // the binding it exports
exp.specifier;
exp.fromName;     // the name a reExport takes
exp.typeOnly;
exp.node;
exp.resolvedFile;
```

## Rename

`binding.rename(name)` renames a binding where it is declared and used, keeping the file's exports.

```js
const file = parse(`export const a = 1;\nlet o = { a };`, { semantic: true });

file.rootScope.find("a").rename("b"); // []
print(file).code;
// const b = 1;
// export { b as a };
// let o = { a: b };
```

When renaming would change what the code means, such as by shadowing or capturing another name, it changes nothing and returns the reasons as [diagnostics](#diagnostics).

## Projects

A `Project` links the imports of many files.

```js
import { Project } from "yuku";

const project = new Project();

project.set("a.ts", `export const value = 1;`);
project.set("b.ts", `export { value as renamed } from "./a.ts";`);
const c = project.set("c.ts", `import { renamed } from "./b.ts"; renamed;`);

c.rootScope.find("renamed").definition().binding.name; // "value"
```

```js
const project = new Project({
  // a path in the project, false for a module outside it, null when it cannot be resolved
  resolve: (specifier, importer) => aliases.get(specifier) ?? null,
});

project.set(path, source, options); // the SourceFile, replacing any at the same path
project.delete(path);
project.files;                      // ReadonlyMap<string, SourceFile>
project.diagnostics;                // every file's, and the links that fail

file.dependencies;       // the files it imports from
file.dependents;         // the files that import it
file.exportedNames();
file.resolveExport("x"); // { file, binding, augmentations }
file.isCurrent;          // false once its path is set again or deleted
```

By default, relative specifiers resolve as TypeScript resolves them, and packages are external.

## Print

`print` turns a file or any node back into code.

```js
import { print } from "yuku";

const { code, map, diagnostics } = print(file, { strip: true, sourceMap: true });
```

| Option      | Default                                 | Description                                                                   |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `strip`     | `false`                                 | Print TypeScript as JavaScript, reporting what has no JavaScript form         |
| `minify`    | `false`                                 | Minify, rewriting syntax to shorter forms such as `!0` and `obj.foo`          |
| `format`    | `"pretty"`, or `"compact"` minifying    | Or `"compact"`                                                                |
| `indent`    | `2`                                     | Spaces per level in the pretty format                                         |
| `quotes`    | `"preserve"`, or `"shortest"` minifying | `"preserve"`, `"double"`, `"single"`, or `"shortest"`                         |
| `comments`  | `"all"`, or `"some"` minifying          | `"all"`, `"some"`, `"none"`, `"line"`, or `"block"`, of the attached comments |
| `sourceMap` | `false`                                 | `true`, or `{ file, sourceRoot, sourcesContent }`, when printing a file       |
| `printers`  | none                                    | Print node types the printer does not know, by `type`                         |

`"some"` keeps legal headers, JSDoc, and `@` or `#` annotations, as bundlers do.

## Performance

`yuku` parses faster than the alternatives on npm, on small and large files.

![Parsing react.js (70 KB) on npm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/react.svg)

![Parsing typescript.js (7.8 MB) on npm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript.svg)

Analyzing a whole codebase, it is faster than typescript-eslint and the TypeScript API, and on a single large file too.

![Analyzing three.js (755 files) on npm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/three.svg)

![Analyzing typescript.js (7.8 MB) on npm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js/refs/heads/main/charts/typescript_js.svg)

Measured on an Apple M3, see the [parser](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-parser-benchmark-js) and [analyzer](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/ecmascript-analyzer-benchmark-js) benchmarks. Pass one `walk` all your visitors.

# Dialects

Source: https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/src/parser/dialect#readme

A dialect adds your own syntax to JavaScript, TypeScript, or JSX, from a single operator to a whole language such as [TSRX](https://tsrx.dev). You write only the new syntax, in one Zig file, compiled into Yuku's parser. Yuku parses, analyzes, walks, and prints the rest of the language to the spec, and your nodes with it, from Zig and from the [`yuku` package](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku/tree/main/npm/yuku#readme).

- [Example](#example)
- [The dialect file](#the-dialect-file): [files](#files), [positions](#positions), [the parser](#the-parser), [nodes](#nodes), [printing](#printing)
- [Analysis, walking, and lowering](#analysis-walking-and-lowering)
- [Building](#building)
- [From JavaScript](#from-javascript)
- [Publishing a package](#publishing-a-package)

## Example

A pipeline operator, `|>`, with `%` as the value piped in.

```zig
// src/pipeline.zig
const std = @import("std");
const yuku = @import("parser");

const ast = yuku.ast;
const dialect = yuku.dialect;
const Error = std.mem.Allocator.Error;

pub const files: []const dialect.File = &.{.{ .extension = ".pipe.js", .lang = .js }};

pub const Node = enum {
    pipeline,
    topic,

    pub fn shape(node: Node) dialect.Shape {
        return switch (node) {
            .pipeline => .{ .type = "PipelineExpression", .fields = &.{ "left", "right" } },
            .topic => .{ .type = "TopicReference" },
        };
    }
};

pub fn operator(p: *dialect.Parser, left: ast.NodeIndex, precedence: u8) Error!dialect.Claim {
    if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, p.tree().source[p.token().span.start..], "|>")) return .decline;
    if (precedence > ast.Precedence.Assignment) return .end;

    if (!try p.advance() or !try p.advance()) return .failed;
    const right = try p.parseExpression(ast.Precedence.Assignment + 1) orelse return .failed;
    const span: ast.Span = .{ .start = p.tree().span(left).start, .end = p.tree().span(right).end };
    return .{ .node = try p.addNode(.pipeline, &.{ left, right }, span) };
}

pub fn expression(p: *dialect.Parser) Error!dialect.Claim {
    const token = p.token();
    if (token.tag != .percent) return .decline;

    if (!try p.advance()) return .failed;
    return .{ .node = try p.addNode(.topic, &.{}, token.span) };
}

pub fn print(w: *dialect.Printer, kind: Node, children: []const ast.NodeIndex) Error!void {
    switch (kind) {
        .pipeline => {
            try w.node(children[0]);
            try w.write(" |> ");
            try w.node(children[1]);
        },
        .topic => try w.write("%"),
    }
}
```

In `prices |> sum(%) |> round(%, 2)`, the pipelines group left to right, the calls inside them are standard nodes, and each pipeline decodes in JavaScript as `{ type: "PipelineExpression", start, end, left, right }`.

## The dialect file

A dialect is a Zig file of public declarations, which imports the parser it is compiled into as `@import("parser")`.

| Declaration        | Required            | Purpose                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `files`            | yes                 | The [files](#files) it reads           |
| `Node`             | to add nodes        | Your [node kinds](#nodes)              |
| Position functions | at least one        | Where your syntax [starts](#positions) |
| `print`            | to print your nodes | How codegen [prints](#printing) them   |

A missing `files`, a function named after no position, a wrong signature, a `Node` without `shape`, or an invalid shape is a compile error. Signatures return exactly `std.mem.Allocator.Error`, not an inferred error set.

### Files

```zig
pub const files: []const dialect.File = &.{
    .{ .extension = ".pipe.js", .lang = .js },
    .{ .extension = ".pipe.ts", .lang = .ts },
};
```

Each entry is a file extension and the standard `lang` it extends. In Zig, a parse opts in with `.dialect = true`, which needs a parser with a dialect compiled in, as `dialect.bound` tells. In JavaScript, the path picks the dialect, see [From JavaScript](#from-javascript).

### Positions

A position is a point in the grammar where the parser asks your dialect first, through the `pub fn` of that name.

| Position           | Called at                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `statement`        | The start of every statement                                                                |
| `expression`       | The start of every operand, before any prefix operator, and at a `@` after `export default` |
| `operator`         | After the operand `left`, where an infix or postfix operator could follow                   |
| `function_body`    | Where a function, method, or arrow function body starts                                     |
| `jsx_child`        | Each JSX child, at byte `offset` in `parent`                                                |
| `jsx_attribute`    | A `{` in a JSX tag, where standard JSX reads a spread attribute                             |
| `jsx_element_name` | The start of an element name, in an opening or closing tag                                  |
| `module_specifier` | A module specifier that is not a string                                                     |

```zig
pub fn statement(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn expression(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn operator(p: *dialect.Parser, left: ast.NodeIndex, precedence: u8) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn function_body(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn jsx_child(p: *dialect.Parser, offset: u32, parent: ast.NodeIndex) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn jsx_attribute(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn jsx_element_name(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
pub fn module_specifier(p: *dialect.Parser) std.mem.Allocator.Error!dialect.Claim
```

| `dialect.Claim`      | Means                                                          |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.decline`           | Not your syntax. Consume no tokens and add no nodes.           |
| `.{ .node = index }` | The node you added, with the current token just past it.       |
| `.failed`            | A diagnostic was reported, by you or by a parse call.          |
| `.end`               | `operator` only. The expression ends before the current token. |

- Positions apply inside your own nodes too, so your syntax and standard syntax nest.
- Decline anything the standard grammar accepts, unless you mean to read it differently.
- `operator` receives the lowest `precedence` that continues the current expression. Answer `.end` when your operator binds more loosely, as the example does.
- `function_body` allows `return` and a directive prologue inside.
- A `jsx_child` node starts at `offset` and ends on its last token, which stays current. `parent` is the opening element or fragment. Call `seek(offset)` first when the child starts with tokens.

### The parser

| `*dialect.Parser`                    | Does                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `token()`                            | The current `ast.Token`                                                                                    |
| `advance()`                          | Moves to the next token, or returns `false` after a lexical error                                          |
| `expect(tag, message)`               | Consumes a token of `tag`, or reports `message` and returns `false`                                        |
| `tokenAt(offset)`                    | The token at or after a byte offset, without moving                                                        |
| `seek(offset)`                       | Makes the token at a byte offset current, at or after the current one                                      |
| `checkpoint()`, `rewind(checkpoint)` | Saves the position as a `dialect.Checkpoint`, and returns to it                                            |
| `semicolon(end)`                     | Ends a statement, with `;` or ASI, returning its end, or null after a diagnostic                           |
| `report(span, message)`              | Reports an error                                                                                           |
| `parseStatement()`                   | Parses a statement                                                                                         |
| `parseExpression(precedence)`        | Parses an expression binding at `precedence` or tighter, `ast.Precedence.Lowest` for a whole one           |
| `parseBindingPattern()`              | Parses an identifier, array, or object pattern, with its type annotation                                   |
| `parseJsxExpressionContainer()`      | Parses the `{ expression }` at the current `{` in a tag                                                    |
| `parseJsxElement()`                  | Parses the element or fragment at the current `<`, leaving its last `>` current                            |
| `addNode(kind, children, span)`      | Adds one of your [nodes](#nodes)                                                                           |
| `list()`                             | A `dialect.List` that collects children of unknown count                                                   |
| `addJsxText(span)`                   | Adds the source text in a non-empty `span` as JSX text                                                     |
| `recordComment(type, span)`          | Records a comment where the standard grammar reads none, in source order                                   |
| `tree()`                             | The `ast.Tree`, to read nodes and [build](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/#building-and-editing) standard ones |

A parse call returns `null` after it reports a diagnostic, and then you answer `.failed`.

```zig
var children = p.list();
defer children.reset();
while (p.token().tag != .right_brace) {
    try children.append(try p.parseStatement() orelse return .failed);
}
const node = try p.addNode(.block, children.items(), span);
```

### Nodes

`Node` is an enum of your node kinds, counting up from 0, whose `shape` describes each one.

```zig
pub const Node = enum {
    each,

    pub fn shape(node: Node) dialect.Shape {
        return switch (node) {
            .each => .{
                .type = "EachStatement",
                .fields = &.{ "item", "list", "body[]" },
                .block_scope = true,
                .lexical_bindings = true,
            },
        };
    }
};
```

| `dialect.Shape`    | Default | Means                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type`             |         | The node's `type` in JavaScript                                                   |
| `fields`           | `&.{}`  | Its children in order, where one name ending in `[]` takes the rest as an array   |
| `properties`       | `"{}"`  | A JSON object of constant properties every node of the kind has in JavaScript     |
| `block_scope`      | `false` | The node opens a block scope                                                      |
| `lexical_bindings` | `false` | Each binding identifier inside declares a `let`-like binding in the current scope |
| `catch_bindings`   | `false` | Each binding identifier inside declares a catch parameter                         |
| `iteration`        | `false` | The node is a loop, which `break` and `continue` end or skip                      |

`addNode` takes children in `fields` order, `.null` for an absent one, lying inside `span`. In the tree, the node is an `ast.Dialect`, its `kind` a `dialect.Kind` and its `children` a range for `tree.extra`. In JavaScript it is a plain object of its `type`, `start`, `end`, fields, and `properties`, so `each (item of list) { ... }` decodes as `{ type: "EachStatement", start, end, item, list, body: [...] }`.

### Printing

```zig
pub fn print(w: *dialect.Printer, kind: Node, children: []const ast.NodeIndex) std.mem.Allocator.Error!void
```

| `*dialect.Printer` | Does                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `write(code)`      | Writes code, with a space before it where needed |
| `space()`          | Writes a space in the pretty format              |
| `node(index)`      | Prints any node, standard or yours               |
| `block(items)`     | Prints a list of statements between braces       |
| `tree()`           | The tree, to read nodes                          |

Without `print`, codegen reports a diagnostic for each of your nodes.

## Analysis, walking, and lowering

Semantic analysis walks into your nodes. Standard code inside them declares, resolves, and reports early errors as usual, and the [shape](#nodes) decides the scope and bindings your node adds. Every [traverser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/) mode reaches your nodes through `enter_dialect` and `exit_dialect`.

```zig
pub fn enter_dialect(self: *Lower, node: ast.Dialect, index: ast.NodeIndex, ctx: *transform.Ctx) traverser.Action
```

To compile your syntax to standard JavaScript, replace each of your nodes with standard ones in a [transform](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/#transform) pass. Every tool then reads plain JavaScript.

## Building

Pass your dialect file to the `yuku` dependency, then build what each side needs.

```zig
// build.zig
const yuku = b.dependency("yuku", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
    .dialect = b.path("src/pipeline.zig"),
});
my_module.addImport("parser", yuku.module("parser"));

b.installArtifact(@import("yuku").addWasm(b, yuku, "pipeline"));
@import("yuku").addAddons(b, yuku);
```

- `yuku.module("parser")` is the Zig parser with your dialect compiled in.
- `addWasm(b, yuku, name)` builds `zig-out/bin/<name>.wasm`, the WebAssembly module the `yuku` package runs: wasm32 with SIMD, optimized for speed, and stripped.
- `addAddons(b, yuku)` builds `zig-out/native/<platform>.node`, the Node-API addon for each platform the package ships, cross-compiled from any machine.

A core compiled without a dialect has no dialect code. With one, a standard file pays one flag check per position, and a dialect file one call. Inside the Yuku repository, `zig build wasm addon -Ddialect=src/pipeline.zig` builds the module and this platform's addon.

## From JavaScript

Make a `Core` from the compiled module and pass it as the `core` option of `parse` or `new Project`. The core is the Zig part those run, so every part of the package then works with your nodes.

```js
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { Core, parse, print } from "yuku";

const wasm = new WebAssembly.Module(readFileSync("zig-out/bin/pipeline.wasm"));
const core = new Core({ wasm });

const file = parse("const total = prices |> sum(%);", { path: "app.pipe.js", core });

print(file, {
  printers: {
    PipelineExpression(node, p) {
      p.node(node.left);
      p.write(" |> ");
      p.node(node.right);
    },
    TopicReference(node, p) {
      p.write("%");
    },
  },
});
```

- A path ending in one of your extensions parses with the dialect, and a source with no path uses the first.
- Any other path, or an explicit `lang`, parses as standard syntax.
- `printers` takes the same calls as `print` in Zig.

Declare your nodes in `DialectNodes` to type them in TypeScript.

```ts
import type { BaseNode, Expression } from "yuku";

declare module "yuku" {
  interface DialectNodes {
    PipelineExpression: BaseNode & { type: "PipelineExpression"; left: Expression; right: Expression };
    TopicReference: BaseNode & { type: "TopicReference" };
  }
}
```

## Publishing a package

A dialect's package ships its core, so its users call `parse` without one.

```ts
import { parse as parseYuku, type ParseOptions, type SourceFile } from "yuku";
import { pipeline } from "#core";

export function parse(source: string, options: Omit<ParseOptions, "core"> = {}): SourceFile {
  return parseYuku(source, { ...options, core: pipeline });
}
```

`#core` gives each runtime its own core, from `package.json`.

```json
"imports": {
  "#core": {
    "workerd": "./dist/core/workerd.js",
    "edge-light": "./dist/core/workerd.js",
    "node": "./dist/core/node.js",
    "default": "./dist/core/default.js"
  }
}
```

| Core              | Runtimes                         | Runs                                                       |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `core/node.ts`    | Node.js, Bun, and Deno           | The addon, and the WebAssembly where no addon loads        |
| `core/workerd.ts` | Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge  | The `.wasm` file, since these cannot compile it from bytes |
| `core/default.ts` | Browsers and every other runtime | The WebAssembly, inlined in base64                         |

```ts
// core/default.ts
import { Core } from "yuku";
import wasm from "../pipeline.wasm"; // in base64, from your bundler

export const pipeline = new Core({ wasm });
```

```ts
// core/node.ts
import { Core } from "yuku";
import wasm from "../pipeline.wasm";

export const pipeline = new Core({
  wasm,
  addons: {
    "darwin-arm64": () => new URL("../native/darwin-arm64.node", import.meta.url),
    "darwin-x64": () => new URL("../native/darwin-x64.node", import.meta.url),
    "linux-arm64": () => new URL("../native/linux-arm64.node", import.meta.url),
    "linux-x64": () => new URL("../native/linux-x64.node", import.meta.url),
    "win32-arm64": () => new URL("../native/win32-arm64.node", import.meta.url),
    "win32-x64": () => new URL("../native/win32-x64.node", import.meta.url),
  },
});
```

Write each addon's URL as its own literal, as above, so bundlers and deploy tracers find the binaries. [yuku-tsrx](https://github.com/yuku-toolchain/yuku-tsrx) is a complete package built this way.
